Plan: all jnanalytics tables on Hugging Face

Source: plan_huggingface.md

Status (2026-11-18): setup done; the code changes (steps 1-8 in the package) are done, untested against BigQuery and Hugging Face. Still to do: dry-run and rebuild of the article tables, export and first upload (step 9).

Goal

One place for the open data: all 15 tables of subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics as Parquet in one Hugging Face dataset repository, versioned per release. The Parquet files are no longer committed to git. The download page, the examples and later the hoaddash dashboard read from Hugging Face.

Decisions

  • All tables on Hugging Face: the six reference tables, the five journal-level aggregates, release, and the article tables articles, article_first_authors and article_agreements.
  • One source: parquet/ stops being committed to git. Older versions stay in the git history.
  • Licence: CC0, as for the package. OpenAlex is CC0; the Crossref metadata used has no reuse restrictions (abstracts are not included, only has_abstract).
  • Namespace (2026-11-18): najkoja/jn_analytics on Hugging Face (personal account; the GitHub repository stays njahn82/jn_analytics).
  • Release tags (2026-11-18): the build date, e.g. 2026-11-17, the same date as in the release table.
  • pub_year column (2026-11-18): article_first_authors and article_agreements get a pub_year column (taken from articles, i.e. the OpenAlex publication year), so all three article tables can be partitioned and exported by year.

Open decisions

  1. DOI: Hugging Face can mint a DOI for a public dataset; minting is a manual step per release. Decide later which releases get one.

Setup (done 2026-11-18)

  1. Public dataset repository najkoja/jn_analytics created (CC0, not gated).
  2. Fine-grained token with read and write access to that repository only, stored as the GitHub secret HF_TOKEN in njahn82/jn_analytics.
  3. Local: hf CLI 2.4.0 via Homebrew, logged in as najkoja for the first upload.

Layout of the dataset repository

README.md                         dataset card (generated)
release.parquet
journals.parquet
journal_issns.parquet
agreements.parquet
agreement_journals.parquet
agreement_institutions.parquet
portfolios.parquet
journal_year.parquet
journal_year_country.parquet
journal_year_license.parquet
journal_year_country_license.parquet
agreement_journal_year.parquet
articles/articles_2016.parquet ... articles_<year_max>.parquet
article_first_authors/article_first_authors_2016.parquet ...
article_agreements/article_agreements_2016.parquet ...
  • Article tables are split by publication year (about 50–100 MB per file; about 1.3 GB in total). Rows of article_first_authors and article_agreements are assigned to the year of their article.
  • Every file carries the schema metadata as now (jn_table, jn_version, jn_columns), written by write_jn_parquet().

Implementation steps

  1. Partition the article tables in BigQuery by pub_year (PARTITION BY RANGE_BUCKET(pub_year, GENERATE_ARRAY(2016, 2100, 1)), or clustering if partitioning does not fit). Then exporting one year scans only that year, and users’ queries filtered by year get cheaper. article_first_authors and article_agreements get a new pub_year column (schema change in inst/schema/columns.csv, the SQL templates, the Rd @format sections and NEWS).
    • Needs a rebuild of the article tables (about 230 GB, about $1.50); best combined with the next quarterly build. Dry-run first.
  2. Export (R/publish.R): extend jn_publish() to write all tables into one folder in the layout above. Article tables are exported year by year with bigrquery (one query per year on the partitioned table, about 9 GB in total). jn_publish_tables() covers all 15 tables.
  3. Dataset card (new internal function, e.g. jn_dataset_card()): generated from jn_schema() and the release table. YAML header with license: cc0-1.0, pretty_name, and one configs entry per table (with data_files patterns) so the Hugging Face viewer shows each table. Body: sources and snapshots, counting rules (link to the data-model page), file list, usage examples.
  4. Upload: hf upload najkoja/jn_analytics <folder> . --repo-type dataset --commit-message "Release <date>", then tag the commit with the release date. Runs with the HF_TOKEN secret. Use hf upload-large-folder if uploads of the article files time out.
  5. Pipeline (_targets.R):
    • export target (format file) after the BigQuery steps, replacing parquet;
    • upload target that reruns only when the exported files changed.
  6. Build workflow (build.yaml): install the Hugging Face CLI (pip install -U huggingface_hub), pass HF_TOKEN, drop parquet/ from the commit step. The check-only mode also checks the token (hf auth whoami).
  7. Git: add parquet/ to .gitignore again and remove it from the index (git rm -r --cached parquet).
  8. Docs:
    • Download page (vignettes/articles/data.Rmd): links to https://huggingface.co/datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/resolve/main/<file>; the release box and file table read release.parquet and the file list from Hugging Face at build time instead of parquet/. New section on the article tables.
    • Examples: DuckDB with hf://datasets/najkoja/jn_analytics/articles/*.parquet, Python (pandas or datasets), R (download, then jn_source()).
    • README “Three ways to the data”, data-model vignette, CLAUDE.md decisions, NEWS.
    • Optional helper jn_download(dir, tables) that fetches files from Hugging Face into a folder for jn_source().
  9. First upload: run the export and upload locally once (dry-run the BigQuery part first), check the dataset viewer and a DuckDB query, then switch the workflow.

Costs

  • Export of the article tables: about 9 GB with partitioning, a few cents. Without partitioning, one query per year would scan the whole table each time (about 50–70 GB in total).
  • Hugging Face hosting of public datasets: free.

Later

  • hoaddash reads the aggregates from Hugging Face.
  • Older releases: keep as tagged revisions on Hugging Face; readers can pin a release with revision=<tag> or .../resolve/<tag>/<file>.
